{{short description|American statistician}}
'''Joanne Roth Wendelberger''' is an American statistician and a scientist at the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]].{{r|lanl}}

==Education and career==
Wendelberger is a 1981 graduate of [[Oberlin College]].{{r|oberlin}} She completed her Ph.D. in 1991 at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]]. Her dissertation, ''Impact, Identification and Estimation of Sources of Transmitted Variation (Propagated Error)'', was supervised by [[George E. P. Box]],{{r|mg}} and her graduate work was also influenced by [[William Hunter (statistician)|William Hunter]] and Brian Joiner.{{r|hunter}}

She joined the Statistical Sciences Group at the Los Alamos National Laboratory in 1992, and became group leader in 2010. She was also deputy division leader for the Computational & Statistical Sciences Division in 2016.{{r|lanl}}

==Recognition==
Wendelberger was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2005.{{r|fasa}}

She is the 2017 winner of the William G. Hunter Award of the Statistics Division of the [[American Society for Quality]], recognizing her promotion of statistical thinking both in her work at the Los Alamos National Laboratory and in local community activism.{{r|hunter}}
